title: Industry Angle Playkit & Prioritization — Fintech / Health / Legal / SaaS / Gov
content:
Purpose and quick summary:
This is a lightweight, tactical playkit to help SDR/AE/SE teams run targeted outreach and pilot conversations across five priority verticals: Fintech, Healthcare, Legal, Enterprise SaaS, and Gov/Defense. Focus is on: 1) one-paragraph positioning, 2) top pain/value props that map to Redwood product levers (latency, cost, private deployment, observability), 3) competitor talking points to neutralize, and 4) sample pilot success metrics and pricing triggers.

Scope and assumptions:
- Audience: mid-market product/infra/ML owners and platform teams for enterprise customers; security/compliance owners for regulated verticals.
- Assumes customers care about cost predictability, SLAs, and ability to run inference close to data.
- Objective: prioritize GTM actions for H1 2025 pilot roster (10 leads per vertical).

How to use this doc:
- SDRs: use the 2-line opener + 30s problem statement under each vertical.
- AEs/SEs: follow the pilot checklist and KPIs to size deals.
- PMM: adapt landing copy experiments and one-pagers.

Topline positioning (single sentence):
"Redwood Inference gives engineering teams production-grade LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private environments so they can ship reliable, predictable, and cost-controlled AI features without wrestling with inference ops."

Vertical play summaries (two-line opener + core props + pilot KPIs)
1) Fintech (payments, lending platforms, wealth/robo-advice)
- Opener: "Reduce inference cost and latencies for real-time fraud/risk signals while keeping models and data within compliant boundaries."
- Core pain mapping:
  - Fraud/risk systems need <200ms tail latencies and predictable throughput (peak shopping/fraud spikes).
  - Data residency and auditability required for compliance.
  - Cost matters for high-volume scoring (per-transaction).
- Redwood hooks to emphasize:
  - Dedicated capacity & latency SLOs for predictable scoring windows.
  - Private deployment option + KMS/HSM integrations for attestation.
  - Cost controls: batching suggestions, quantization profiles for scorer models.
- Competitor notes / rebuttals:
  - Cloud providers: strong on scale but customers complain about unpredictable per-call costs and opaque tail latencies. Emphasize predictable reserved capacity + SLOs.
  - LLM API pure-play: easier to start but lacks private deployments and audit controls. Push on security + private control plane.
- Pilot KPIs (example): 1) 30% reduction in per-score cost via batching/quantization; 2) 95th percentile latency below 200ms under production load; 3) successful KMS integration + audit trail.
- Pricing trigger: commit to reserved nodes if avg monthly scoring volume > X (include template calculation in playbook).

2) Healthcare (clinical decision support, patient messaging, prior auth)
- Opener: "Enable regulated teams to use LLMs for clinician/operational workflows while preserving PHI security and auditability."
- Core pain mapping:
  - PHI/hospital data cannot be sent to multi-tenant hosted providers in many cases.
  - Explainability, reproducibility, and model versioning are required for clinical validation.
  - Ops teams wary of silent quality regressions.
- Redwood hooks:
  - Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment and audit logs; model pinning and rollout controls for validation.
  - Observability: per-route token cost, latency, model drift alerts tied to eval sets.
  - Rollout policies (canary, A/B) for safe model updates.
- Competitor notes / rebuttals:
  - Enterprise cloud AI: may offer VPC, but rollout and eval tooling is lightweight. Call out Redwood Optimize and quality-monitoring tied to prompt sets.
  - On-prem inference vendors: need integration work; we offer dev-friendly API parity across environments.
- Pilot KPIs: 1) validate audit chain for PHI pipelines; 2) run clinical eval suite with no regression vs baseline; 3) <5% model drift alerts over 60d.

3) Legal (e-discovery, contract analytics, counsel automation)
- Opener: "Speed up legal review loops with reliable, auditable inference and deterministic model rollouts so legal ops can own risk."
- Core pain mapping:
  - Traceability for outputs, model provenance, and versioned rollbacks are top asks.
  - Latency less critical than reproducibility and exportable logs.
  - Integration into corp DMS (document stores) and enterprise SSO/KMS.
- Redwood hooks:
  - Full audit logs + model pinning + deterministic inference paths (cache controls).
  - Private deployment options for legal firms or corp-legal.
  - Exportable reports and eval dashboards for legal ops.
- Competitor notes / rebuttals:
  - Legal tech companies: may bake models into workflows but often lack enterprise-grade observability and capacity guarantees—our angle is operational reliability.
- Pilot KPIs: 1) reproducible results for three canonical contract templates; 2) time-to-first-review reduced by 40%; 3) legal ops signoff on audit exports.

4) Enterprise SaaS (product teams adding in-app AI features)
- Opener: "Ship AI features fast with predictable inference economics and integrated observability to protect margins."
- Core pain mapping:
  - Product teams need low friction (SDKs, streaming) + predictable unit economics to make feature decisions.
  - Need feature flagging/rollouts and simple model swaps for experiments.
- Redwood hooks:
  - Hosted API for fast time-to-value and Dedicated for growth with committed capacity.
  - SDKs + function calling / structured output to reduce SE integration time.
  - Cost dashboards at token/route level for PM finance alignment.
- Competitor notes / rebuttals:
  - LLM API players: best for MVPs but costs scale and fallbacks are manual. We provide clear upgrade path to Dedicated + optimize toolkit.
- Pilot KPIs: 1) time-to-integration < 2 weeks; 2) cost per active user below target threshold; 3) rollback/variant experiment executed without prod incidents.

5) Gov / Defense (classified adjacency, regulated procurement)
- Opener: "Support sensitive deployments with optional air-gapped/private control plane and procurement-friendly SLAs."
- Core pain mapping:
  - Procurement cycles long; security and compliance checkboxes are decisive.
  - Need hardened attestations, HSM/KMS, and optional on-prem packages.
- Redwood hooks:
  - Private deployment + on-prem packaged offer; enterprise support and SOC2/ISO tooling.
  - Enterprise sales support for procurement/contract language + SOW templates.
- Competitor notes / rebuttals:
  - Big cloud providers: strong but heavy procurement; offer Redwood as simpler packaged on-prem alternative with faster integration.
- Pilot KPIs: 1) pass initial security questionnaire; 2) successful on-prem deployment in staging; 3) procurement milestone reached (e.g., PO issued).

Cross-vertical play levers (how to map product features to revenue motions)
- Hosted -> Try & Buy (freemium credits) for quick evaluation. Use prebuilt connectors and SDK guides.
- Dedicated -> Growth conversion; focus engineering case studies and TCO (total cost of ownership) calculators.
- Private -> Enterprise contract motion; highlight compliance, KMS, and audit logs.
- Redwood Optimize -> Upsell for cost-sensitive, high-throughput customers (show projected savings).
- Redwood Console -> Expand into platform teams who need observability and tracing.

Competitive landscape shorthand (one-line each)
- Hyperscalers: scale + trust but opaque tail latencies and complex contracts.
- LLM API startups: fastest to start, weakest for private/compliance controls.
- Self-host inference vendors: deep customization but heavy ops burden—our pitch is low lift + ops-grade runtime.

Recommended GTM experiments (H1 2025)
- Fintech: run a "score-at-scale" benchmark kit and publish anonymized results vs typical cloud endpoint costs. Use a conversion path: benchmark -> pilot -> reserved capacity quote. Measure conversion rate.
- Healthcare: 1 clinical partner pilot with model pinning + audit exports; create a short playbook for clinical validation.
- Legal: field a microsite with contract-analysis battlecard and offer a 30-day reproducibility audit as a lead magnet.
- Enterprise SaaS: 2-week integration hackathon program (free SE hours + onboarding template) to create case studies.
- Gov/Defense: package an on-prem mini-sprint SOW and outreach to channel partners who already serve this vertical.

Sales enablement assets to create (priority order)
1) Vertical one-pagers (2-sided): top problems + how Redwood maps to them + pilot success metrics.
2) Playbook scripts for SDRs: 2-line opener + 30s problem + 1-sentence credibility.
3) Pilot checklist + SOW template for private deployments.
4) TCO calculators for Dedicated conversions.
5) Security FAQ tailored for procurement and infosec reviewers.

Measurement plan (what to track)
- Leads created per vertical and conversion rate to pilot.
- Pilot success rate (met KPIs) and time to decision.
- ACV uplift after Dedicated/Private conversion.
- Average token cost delta pre/post Optimize.

Open questions / outstanding decisions
- Pricing floor for short-term private pilots (what is minimum MRR we accept?). TODO: finance to confirm (see jira:GTM-1123).
- Should we bundle Optimize in early Dedicated deals as a promo? Pros/cons to experiment.
- What security artifacts to pre-generate for gov RFPs vs bespoke pack? (SE input required)

Immediate next steps (owners)
- Create fintech benchmark kit (Julian) — due 2025-02-28.
- Draft healthcare clinical-validation one-pager (Maya) — due 2025-03-08.
- Build legal reproducibility microsite skeleton (Aisha) — due 2025-03-05.
- Finance: confirm private pilot pricing floor (Samir) — due 2025-02-25.

Appendix: sample SDR openers (copy-ready)
- Fintech: "Quick question — do you have a scoring endpoint for fraud that hits tail-latency issues during spikes? We help teams guarantee <200ms 95th percentile with reserved inference capacity and audited private deployment if needed."
- Healthcare: "Are you comfortable sending PHI to a multi-tenant model provider? We run private deployments with full audit logs and evaluation gating used by clinical teams."
- Legal: "Can your legal ops export model provenance for specific contract reviews? We provide versioned rollouts + audit exports to satisfy legal compliance."

Notes to self / rough ideas for collateral
- Landing page: interactive cost calculator where users enter transactions/day -> shows recommended mode (hosted/dedicated/private) and estimated monthly bill.
- Case study template: problem, infra baseline, Redwood intervention (batching/quantization/routing), measured savings.
